headline: Approved $6,400 and $400 from memorial funds to upgrade cadet program radios; also approved state highway safety grant applications.
summary: Speakers commented on the city's LPR and automated camera program and the Bristol Police Department Internship Program. Members approved the cadet radio funding, a parking waiver for Marwood Condominiums, and applying for state highway safety grants. They also directed a request to the CT DOT for a study of heavy truck use on Willis Street.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the August 18, 2026 regular meeting, unanimously.
Approved the minutes of the August 24, 2026 special meeting, 6-1, with Commissioner Ghio abstaining.
Approved the minutes of the August 31, 2026 special meeting, 6-1, with Mayor Zoppo-Sassu abstaining.
Approved the minutes of the September 8, 2026 special meeting, 5-2, with Mayor Zoppo-Sassu and Commissioner Kilbourne abstaining.
Approved the monthly reports and placed them on file, unanimously.
Approved an additional appropriation of $6,400 from the Sergeant Alex Hamzy Memorial Fund and $400 from the Rafi Hamzy Fund for cadet program radio upgrades, unanimously.
Approved the parking waiver request from Marwood Condominiums for December 15, 2026 through March 15, 2027, unanimously.

Approved applying for and accepting, if awarded, the distracted driving high visibility enforcement grant, DUI enforcement grant, and speed and aggressive driving grant from the State of CT DOT, unanimously.
Approved directing Traffic Lieutenant Lang Mussen to request that the CT DOT study heavy truck use on Willis Street and make recommendations, unanimously.

plain_text:
BOARD OF POLICE COMMISSIONERS 
REGULAR MEETING 
                                                      SEPTEMBER 16, 2026, AT 6:00 p.m. 
COUNCIL CHAMBERS 
 
PRESENT:             ABSENT:  
Mayor Ellen Zoppo-Sassu, Chairperson            
Commissioner Rory Ghio 
Commissioner Dean Kilbourne         
Commissioner Paul Lemieux 
Commissioner Terry Lewis 
Commissioner Gloria Sapp Smith 
Council Member Sue Tyler               
Board of Finance Liaison, Jon Mace 
 
1. CALL TO ORDER 
Mayor Zoppo-Sassu called the meeting to order at 6:00 P.M. 
 
2. PRESENTATION OF AWARDS 
No Awards. 
  
3. PUBLIC PARTICIPATION 
Nick Palmer, 69 Cronin Street, spoke in opposition to the City’s LPR and automated camera program. 
 
Detective Travisano and Officer Kichar spoke regarding the Bristol Police Department Internship 
Program. 
 
 
4. APPROVAL OF MINUTES 
Council Member Tyler moved to APPROVE THE MINUTES FROM THE AUGUST 18, 2026, 
REGULAR POLICE BOARD MEETING, seconded by Commissioner Kilbourne. 
 
VOTE: UNANIMOUSLY PASSED  
 
Commissioner Sapp-Smith moved to APPROVE THE MINUTES FROM THE AUGUST 24, 2026 
SPECIAL POLICE BOARD MEETING, seconded by Commissioner Lemieux. 
 
VOTE: PASSED (6-1. Commissioner Ghio abstained) 
 
Commissioner Ghio moved to APPROVE THE MINUTES FROM THE AUGUST 31, 2026 SPECIAL 
POLICE BOARD MEETING, seconded by Council Member Tyler. 
 
VOTE: PASSED (6-1. Mayor Zoppo-Sassu abstained)  
 
Commissioner Lewis moved to APPROVE THE MINUTES FROM THE SEPTEMBER 8, 2026 
SPECIAL POLICE BOARD MEETING, seconded by Commissioner Ghio.   
 
VOTE: PASSED (5-2. Mayor Zoppo-Sassu and 
Commissioner Kilbourne abstained.
5. APPROVAL OF VARIOUS MONTHLY REPORTS 
Commissioner Lewis moved to APPROVE MONTHLY REPORTS AND PLACE ON FILE, seconded 
by Commissioner Lemieux. 
 
              VOTE: UNANIMOUSLY PASSED 
 
6. CORRESPONDENCE 
Mayor Zoppo-Sassu received two Facebook communications, one from Diane Zibold from Holley Road 
concerning the increase in traffic on Woodland Street hill. The second one is from Morgan Murphy 
concerning the intersection of Morris and Louisiana for the high school walkers.  She requested a zone 
car check at that intersection occasionally between 7:00 am and 7:30 am. 
 
 
7. COMMITTEE MINUTES 
No committee reports. 
 
8. OLD BUSINESS 
8.1  Chief Morello 
None 
 
8.2     Police Commissioners 
None 
 
9.  NEW BUSINESS 
9.1   Chief Morello 
i. Chief’s Report 
Chief Morello reviewed the Chief's report. 
 
ii. Board of Finance Request 
Commissioner Kilbourne moved to APPROVE THE ADDITIONAL APPROPRIATION REQUEST 
OF $6,400 FROM THE SERGEANT ALEX HAMZY MEMORIAL FUND AND $400 FROM THE 
RAFI HAMZY FUND TO SUPPORT THE CADET PROGRAM TO UPGRADE RADIOS, seconded 
by Council Member Tyler. 
 
              VOTE: UNANIMOUSLY PASSED 
 
iii. Marwood Condominiums Parking Waiver Request 
Commissioner Ghio moved to APPROVE THE PARKING WAIVER REQUEST FROM MARWOOD 
CONDOMINIUMS FROM DECEMBER 15, 2026 THROUGH MARCH 15, 2027, seconded by 
Commissioner Lewis. 
 
              VOTE: UNANIMOUSLY PASSED 
 
iv. State of CT DOT Highway Safety Grants 
Commissioner Ghio moved to APPROVE APPLYING FOR AND PERMISSION TO ACCEPT THE 
FOLLOWING GRANTS IF AWARDED: DISTRACTED DRIVING HIGH VISIBILITY 
ENFORCEMENT GRANT, DUI ENFORCEMENT GRANT AND SPEED & AGGRESSIVE 
DRIVING GRANT, seconded by Council Member Tyler.
VOTE: UNANIMOUSLY PASSED 
 
v. To direct Traffic Lieutenant Lang Mussen to request that the CT DOT conduct a study and make 
recommendations regarding the use of heavy trucks on Willis Street, including, but not restricting such 
use by heavy vehicles and providing alternative routes. 
 
Commissioner Lemieux moved to DIRECT LIEUTENANT LANG MUSSEN TO REQUEST THAT 
THE CT DOT CONDUCT A STUDY AND MAKE RECOMMENDATIONS REGARDING THE USE 
OF HEAVY TRUCKS ON WILLIS STREET, INCLUDING, BUT NOT RESTRICTING SUCH USE 
BY HEAVY VEHICLES AND PROVIDING ALTERNATIVE ROUTES, seconded by Commissioner 
Ghio. 
 
              VOTE: UNANIMOUSLY PASSED 
 
vi. Crosswalks on Wolcott Street near BCHS 
Chief Morello will reach out to the SRO for input and email the response so the information is available 
for the Public Works meeting.  
 
9.2 Police Commissioners 
No new business. 
 
 
10. ADJOURNMENT 
Commissioner Sapp-Smith moved to ADJOURN, Seconded by Commissioner Lemieux.  
  
             VOTE: UNANIMOUSLY PASSED  
 
 
The regular meeting of the Board of Police Commissioners called for the 16th day of SEPTEMBER, 
2026, was HEREBY ADJOURNED AT 6:37 p.m. 
 
 
 
                   Lisa Ziogas                   Recording Secretary
